speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The horn is empty enough to insult a man. Sit, and eat, and then tell me whether you will have it filled or whether you will write in water.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fill it. Twopence, as you sell it. Yesterday's spoon has done its work in the galls. I would like a horn that has not been a quarrel.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The spoon is soaking. The black is still in the neck. I told you it would not wipe. The horn is the clean one, from the cupboard, not from the basket.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Twopence, then. And threepence if you are eating, which you are, because the bread is already in your hand. I am not running a charity for poets who hover.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Threepence. I am eating. The loaf is still short by a finger, and I am still not arguing with the baker.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Your letter is where you left it. Folded. Thursday. If you open it this morning to put a day into it, you will be late for your own play and no more honest than you were on Sunday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not opening it. The day of coming is not in it, and Thursday is soon enough for a sheet that was true on Septuagesima. I will not improve a truth into a promise.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Is there news in it of your father? Mistress said last time he was mending. Mending is not the same as well. I ask because the cough was in the other letter, and this one is fat enough to have an answer.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: This one is mine, going, not hers, coming. I have no newer word than mending. When Hobbins brings a sheet, I will know. I will not guess a man's breath from a folded page of my own.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Good. Guessing is how spoons become thefts. Twopence is on the horn. You may take it up with you, and you may bring it down empty at the end of the week, and I will fill it again at the same price.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The copperas is in the pot, measured. I used a stick this morning, not a spoon. Mistress kept her eye on the stick as if it might grow a handle and a guilty look.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I kept my eye on a stick because yesterday I had used the wrong tool and accused the stair. A Christian woman can learn a thing before noon on a Monday. Eat your bread.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am eating it. At two I am Navarre, in a paper crown, and the crown is on the peg upstairs. Old velvet over it. The yard will not know the velvet is old if I do not tell them.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: May I see the crown before you go? I will not put it on. Mistress says a paper crown in a kitchen becomes a spill, and then a lecture.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You may see it from the door, and not from a stool. Master Shakespeare, the Inns were loud on Thursday, Alse says, through the floor. If they are loud again today, I shall hear them from here and I shall not be pleased to be right.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: If they are loud, Garnish will have a number for it by the time I am home, and the number will be lines, not shillings. I am not bringing the boxes back to this table.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Lines are the ones Master Kemp puts in that are not in the book. I heard that much through the floor. I have not heard how many.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thursday was eleven. Today is not Thursday. Do not spend eleven at breakfast as if it were a sum you could buy bread with.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Eleven lines will not pay the threepence. The threepence is paid. The twopence is paid. Go up for the crown when you have finished, and come down with your face in order. I am not sending a king into Gracechurch Street with crumbs in his beard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No crumbs. No new sentence in the letter. A full horn, and a paper crown, and two of the clock. That is the morning's list, and it is short on purpose.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will set the horn by the stair so you do not go without it. A player with no ink is only a man who talks.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: And a landlady with no twopence is a woman out of pocket. I have the twopence. Master Shakespeare, if your father is worse than mending, the carrier will say so. You will not get it out of me, because I have not got it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I know. Thursday. Until Thursday he is mending, and the sheet on the table does not know any more than I do.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Mending is a good enough word for a Monday. I will not ask it again before Thursday. I might ask about the crown.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Ask about the crown at the door, and then let me go. The horn is yours until I am on the stair. After that it is mine, at twopence, and I mean to empty it honestly.
